reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify shared structural patterns across misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantitatively assess feature attributions and spurious correlations. This approach enhances detection of spurious features by leveraging both pattern recognition and model-level attribution scores, ensuring robustness and statistical validity.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which columns are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 9686) and check for features that are semantically unrelated to income prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: List of shared categorical or numerical features across all three instances that are not semantically meaningful in relation to income class

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status, relationship) appears to correlate with misclassification due to a spurious pattern (e.g., 'Married-civ-spouse' with 'Husband' relationship), despite lacking direct causal or semantic link to income.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Hypothesis about a spurious feature-driven bias, such as over-reliance on relationship or marital status due to data distribution or correlation with income in training

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides interpretable, model-agnostic feature importance scores across all instances, allowing us to detect which features have high attribution in misclassifications. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local explanations to validate regional importance and gradient-based spurious signals. Sensitivity analysis isolates feature impact by ablation, confirming whether removing a shared feature alters predictions—critical for detecting spuriousness. Together, they validate autonomous hypotheses with statistical rigor.
